Hosted job log is in. systemd (pid 1) sent the SIGTERM after one OOM kill, and swap was full. I'm parsing the memory curve now.

Confirmed the hosted mechanism matches the local one. I'm checking why the records upload was skipped, then I'll post the hosted note and close the bead.

I closed bead sase-1rq.2.1.4.1.1. The hosted Telemetry run (run 42397793381, job 128482929439, on the diagnostics commit `f97019e7e8`) died the same way as the local reproduction. Memory ran out while the 26 workers were still collecting tests, the kernel killed one process, and systemd then stopped the whole runner with SIGTERM. No test ever ran.

**Hosted run:** Python 3.12.16 on a 4-CPU runner with 15.6 GB of RAM and 3.0 GB of swap. The test workers were pinned to CPUs 0–1, and the runner's service had no memory limit of its own.
- **Collection:** after 27m53s, none of the 26 workers had finished collecting. CPU pressure stayed near 98% for most of the run, so each worker needs more than about 99 CPU-seconds to collect on this runner. Locally on Python 3.14 it took 57.
- **Memory:** the test processes grew steadily (4.9 GB at 2 min, 11.0 GB at 12 min, 15.4 GB at 21 min), peaking at about 15.6 GB, roughly 600 MB per worker. Free memory reached 0.1 GB at +1367 s and swap was full at +1582 s. After that the machine thrashed: about 12 GiB swapped out and 11 GiB back in.
- **Kill sequence:** one out-of-memory kill happened between +1659 s and +1673 s. At +1673 s, systemd (pid 1, root) sent SIGTERM from outside the test processes. The runner logged "received a shutdown signal" 0.2 s later, and its cleanup then terminated 25 leftover python processes. A gap in their pid sequence suggests the killed process was one worker, but that is a guess.
- **Disk:** ruled out, with at least 84.5 GB and 18.4M inodes free.

**What the fix phase (sase-1rq.2.1.4.1.2) has to change:** the memory and CPU of 26 workers each collecting the full test selection on two CPUs. Total collection memory must stay well under about 15 GB. Changing how tests handle signals can't help, because systemd stops the runner from outside.

**Still unknown:**
- which process was killed for memory;
- how the runner's service is configured to react to an out-of-memory kill (the sender and timing match "stop the whole unit");
- the full per-worker collection memory and CPU on Python 3.12;
- whether the 25 leftover workers ignored SIGTERM or were just slow to die while thrashing.

**Gaps in the diagnostics:**
- The step that uploads the contention records was skipped when the runner shut down, even though it is set to always run. The job log was the only hosted evidence, which is why the sampler prints its lines there.
- The progress line showed "0/25 workers" although pytest created 26. A throttled progress write dropped the 26th, so the "25 configured" in the earlier local note is the same artifact.

**Bead notes:** I posted an `EVIDENCE (hosted, …)` note with the numbers above, plus one `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP` for the worker-count write. The earlier follow-up about the sampler losing track of the test processes once their root dies was seen again here. No epic symbols remained, no repository files changed, and the host required no commit declaration.
